n: James speaks like an Old Testament prophet to rich oppressors: weep and wail, for misery is coming. The warning targets those who gained wealth by injustice.
Their hoarded wealth is already rotting and their fine clothes are eaten by moths. Earthly treasure does not last.
Their gold and silver are corroded, and that corrosion will testify against them. They piled up riches even as the last days were drawing near.

f.g: Corroded, rusted (gold doesn’t literally rust—James is making a moral point).

n: The wages they cheated from their harvest workers cry out, and God—the Lord of armies—has heard those cries.
They lived in luxury and self-indulgence, fattening themselves like cattle—unaware that it was a day of slaughter for them.
They condemned and killed innocent people who did not fight back. Many readers also see here the Righteous One, Jesus, who submitted without resistance.
To the oppressed believers James says: be patient until the Lord comes. A farmer waits for the autumn and spring rains before the harvest.

f.g: In Palestine the early rain falls in autumn after sowing; the latter rain in spring before harvest.

n: So be patient and strengthen your hearts; the Lord’s coming is near.
Don’t grumble against each other in hard times. The Judge is already standing at the door, ready to enter.
Look to the prophets as models of patiently suffering hardship while faithfully speaking for the Lord.
We call people blessed who endure. Job’s steadfastness shows how the Lord in the end proved full of compassion and mercy.
Echoing Jesus, James says not to swear oaths to back up what you say. Be so honest that a simple yes or no is enough.
In every situation, turn to God: pray in trouble, sing praises in happy times.
Anyone sick should call the Church elders to pray over him and anoint him with oil in the Lord’s name. Latter-day Saints still follow this pattern in priesthood blessings of the sick.

f.g: Olive oil, consecrated and applied in the Lord’s name.

n: Prayer offered in faith will help the sick person, and the Lord will raise him up. Forgiveness of sins is also offered—healing of body and soul go together.
Admit your faults to one another and pray for each other so you can be healed. The earnest prayer of a righteous person is powerful.
Elijah was an ordinary human like us, yet his prayer closed the heavens for three and a half years. Ordinary people can pray with extraordinary faith.

f.g: Greek form of the name Elijah.

n: When Elijah prayed again, rain came and the land produced crops once more.
If a believer wanders from the truth and someone helps bring him back,
that rescuer saves a soul from spiritual death and helps cover many sins. James ends his letter on the joy of rescuing the lost.
